## Exact raw contract

Three simultaneous, unfiltered RGBA32F outputs are used at locations/attachments
0, 1, 2 → colortex9, 10, 11. Every count is an integer in 0–16,777,215 and is
exactly representable in binary32. Overflow is sticky and outputs all `-1`.
The dedicated bound uniform `shaderlodVolumeLightRateDiagnosticSchema` must be
1; otherwise every page is all `-1`.

| Page | RGBA channels |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | primary density calls N; occupied primary cells Q; reused secondary pairs R; executed secondary density calls S |
| 1 | configured lighting steps L; configured ambient steps A; actual mode; actual path |
| 2 | schema 1; diagnostic marker 713001; valid 1; reserved 0 |

N increments immediately before each reached primary density call, after the
unchanged transmittance break. Q increments after the original empty-density
continue and before original distance fade. R increments only inside the actual
`if (reuse_lighting)` branch that takes cached depths and executes neither
secondary kernel. S increments immediately before each reached density call
inside the original or private optical-depth loop. These are function-call
counts; density can return before issuing texture fetches. They are not physical
texture issues, wavefront activity, latency or GPU time.

Modes: 0 private light-rate OFF; 1 core/global fallback; 2 sampling-only; 3
reuse-enabled. Paths: 0 cumulus draw not called; 1 literal original draw; 2
private draw. Mode 3 with R = 0 means reuse was configured but none of the
sampled ray's reached cells took reuse. It does not mean missing data when the
same ray has valid schema/marker. Path 0 means the cumulus draw was not called;
zero counts must not be interpreted as a hit with no work. Counter validity only
certifies no counter overflow and a bound diagnostic schema; it is not a finite
lighting/output or scene certification.

For a captured valid ray, require `N >= Q >= R >= 0` and
`S = (Q - R) × (L + A)`, with `R = 0` for modes 0–2. A sampled `R > 0` under
mode 3/path 2 is direct observation of a reached branch skipping complete
secondary kernels in that instrumented draw. It does not establish whole-screen
coverage, causal paired work savings, quality, driver speed or normal-candidate
performance. Reject absent captures, sentinels, wrong marker or inconsistent
accounting rather than relabel them zero reuse.

Do not use full output dimensions as the diagnostic ray grid. Other upscale
settings retain their original 1, 1/2 or approximately 1/3 cloud extents. The
normal footprint guard still uses full output `view_res`, unchanged by tracing.


Default outputs are ignored `build/volume-light-rate-diagnostic-enabled-on.zip`
and its registration sidecar. `--arm sampling --trace` and

Use the [higher-sun plan](PHOTON_DAYLIGHT_SCENE_PLAN.md) to copy/freeze a fresh

window/focus/camera and raw capture. The sunset low-sun guard remains unchanged.
The sidecar requests an 8 × 8 grid, up to eight captures spaced 60 matching draws
apart. This samples at most 512 rays; no positive R in those samples does not
prove zero whole-screen reuse. Positive R establishes sampled activation only.
Normal candidate still/motion quality must be inspected separately because raw
counts overwrite cloud color/history. Stop quickly on negligible sampled reuse
or conspicuous normal-arm shadow, edge or motion artifacts.

Only an active, visually acceptable normal candidate merits repeated matched
original/private-OFF/sampling/reuse total-frame GPU and frame-throughput timing,
with equal hardware, exact revision/artifacts, effective settings, fresh input
scene, resolution/focus, warmup and qualified temporal state. Separately qualify
cloud-pass intervals if collected. Diagnostic timings are invalid. No performance
claim can follow without measured baseline and optimized normal GPU timings.
This worker stops at source qualification and precise capture handoff; no
production promotion or project completion is claimed.

## Sampling, overlap and resolution safeguards

This M3 runtime previously reported timestampBits=0, elapsedBits=32,
ELAPSED_ALTERNATING. Recheck actual backend/counters; do not infer support from
OpenGL version. Seven-category frames are FRAME, IRIS, TERRAIN, DH_DRAW,
DH_TOTAL, BUFFER_DRAWS and RENDER_AND_BLIT. Each category recurs every `7*N`
runTick frames, not every N. In no-DH coastal runs, the two DH categories still
consume schedule slots. Do not classify missing DH records as zero submitted
work. At 50–60 FPS and N=5, a 60s capture provides roughly 86–103 opportunities
per category; actual successful counts, drops and pending results decide usability.

For cloud upscale4, `d1_clouds.fsh:128,162` uses frameCounter modulo16 for
checkerboard offset; `:208` advances outer noise by frameCounter/16. N=16 can
repeatedly query one offset. Seven-category N=5 recurs at35 frames, coprime to16
**if** Iris frameCounter and measured runTick frames advance one-to-one.
Use existing phase frameCounter/frameId boundaries to check that assumption;
they do not expose every queried frame's exact shader counter. Label this an
alias-reduction diagnostic, not proven full coverage. Two-category recurrence
is `2*N`, always even, so each IRIS scope can sample only a subset of16 offsets.
Do not prefer its denser statistics without acknowledging that limitation.

There is no nested elapsed decomposition. FRAME, pass and terrain records come
from different frames. DH-total contains DH draws; shadow-map contains shadow
terrain; CPU game-render contains terrain/Iris/driver submission; execute-batch
contains native draw-submit. **Do not sum parents and children, sum different
category medians, or subtract pass totals from game-render as driver cost.**
Elapsed intervals include command starvation/scheduling and tile effects; the
unmarked gaps between leaf passes are not measured GPU busy/idle time.
The [Khronos timer specification](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/extensions/ARB/ARB_timer_query.txt)
defines completion timing, non-nesting elapsed queries and tile-order caveats.

Keep zero results, zero fraction and minimum positive result visible. A zero
median for deferred sky or a small cloud pass is unresolved timer granularity,
not proof of cache/free work. It also does not license adding synthetic workload.
The sky program executes in source; no pixel parity or meaningful clock precision
follows from its tiny query values. Ring drops, stale epochs, missing backend,
GL errors or query shutdown invalidate attribution rather than becoming zero cost.

## Signed range and other formats

Nonnegative physical radiance is not a complete shader range proof. R11 loses
negative stored components and reduces mantissa precision. No actual pixel
range was measured by this worker. Alpha alone already decisively rejects the
large RGBA16F targets, so this report does not pretend to prove their HDR ranges
or temporal quality.

Sky4 has two further boundaries. SH is off in these maps, so the compute producer
must not be blamed as current work. If enabled elsewhere,
`d4a_generate_sky_sh.csh:18,85–101,142` binds an rgba16f image and writes signed
SH coefficients. `utility/spherical_harmonics.glsl:25–36` has basis terms with
both signs, so a global unsigned format replacement is invalid for that graph.
Even with SH off, `sky/atmosphere.glsl:106–114` extrapolates atmosphere saturation
without max0. The effective intensity is 1; `shaders.properties` supplies a
1.10–1.30 boost at line 501. Algebraically, sufficiently low channels can become negative;
this is a source possibility, **not observed negative pixels**. d0 does not
clamp the final sky-map store. Its consumers include reflection filtering and
light-color palettes, so clipping cannot be presumed harmless.

Fog7 is RGB16F already, not an RGBA alpha-drop candidate. It is quarter-area,
`shaders.properties:256`, and c0 writes fresh scattering each frame rather than
blending its own previous value. The old fog is nevertheless consumed by SSR:
`lighting/specular_lighting.glsl:256–285` subtracts previous scattering from
previous scene color then clamps the difference before applying current analytic
fog. Quantization can affect that cancellation. `c0_vl.fsh:198–199` writes raw
raymarched scattering; `fog/overworld/raymarched.glsl:197–219` incorporates
ambient/light colors without a final max0. `lighting/colors/light_color.glsl:62`
calls the saturation extrapolation above. Thus unsigned safety is unproved even
in the effective Overworld VL path. Its deferred-stage colortex7 alias is a
custom 3-D noise image (`shaders.properties:351`), not this composite attachment.
Target12 stores cloud distance/age/indirect scattering, target10 stores cloud
distance/indirect scattering, and targets14/15 carry AO/depth data; these are
outside the permitted simple radiance precision replacement. No packing changes
are proposed.

## OpenGL boundary and next action

The [OpenGL 4.1 core specification](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/specs/gl/glspec41.core.pdf)
lists R11F_G11F_B10F among required texture/renderbuffer color formats
(printed pp. 196–197). RGB16F and RGB9_E5 are in its texture-only required list,
so one cannot assume RGB9_E5 is a portable four-byte attachment substitute.
R11's unsigned storage and missing alpha follow the format definition.

The [Khronos packed-float definition](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/extensions/EXT/EXT_packed_float.txt)
specifies 6/6/5 mantissa bits, 5 exponent bits, no sign, sampled alpha=1 and
negative-to-zero conversion. This creates explicit quality risks for signed
values, cancellation and repeated temporal quantization. A legal format does
not prove a particular Iris framebuffer is complete or fast.

Even the tiny sky-map possibility changes only 82,944 nominal bytes per physical
image (192 × 108 × four bytes). This is component-size arithmetic, **not measured
bus traffic, actual allocation, bandwidth or a time saving**. Texture cache,
padding, driver tiling/compression and repeated reads are not measured here.
No large target with unused alpha qualifies, so there is no requested candidate
to implement or time. The practical next action is to close this lane and keep
the root's existing sample/work-avoidance experiments. Reopen only if a different
adapter exposes a large, nonnegative RGB-only HDR attachment with complete
producer/consumer/blend/clear/history proof; first use a query-free actual-format
and still/motion quality control, then a short matched timing screen.

## Algebra and rendering semantics

Each B15 secondary optical-depth call initializes its base `step_length` using
the selected count. If selected and original counts differ, it multiplies by:

```glsl
(float(step_count) / float(original_steps)) *
    (exp2(float(original_steps)) - 1.0) / (exp2(float(step_count)) - 1.0)
```

Selected lighting and ambient counts are finalized by the existing mode/preset
selection before the primary march and never assigned inside it. Original
counts are compile-time pack options. This ratio therefore depends on neither
primary sample position nor secondary jitter, density, direction or sun time.
It is dimensionless. The probe evaluates this exact, left-associated expression
once for light and once for sky after final count selection, then passes the
values into the secondary function. Neither count division is cancelled, and
the expression is not changed to an equivalent differently rounded formula.

Each caller computes its ratio only under its explicit
`selectedCount != originalCount` guard. Extent variables initialize to 1.0, but
the optical-depth function retains the original inequality branch, so full-count
paths perform no identity multiplication. The secondary base-length division
and any altocumulus sunrise/sunset factor remain in the original function.
Equal-count near/tier-zero/live-disabled paths retain original count, initial
length and sample math. The full compile-time `SHADERLOD_CLOUDS`-off source tail
is untouched, and continues selecting the original Photon functions.

Primary origin, jitter, loop count, density ordering, transmittance break and
empty-sample skip are unchanged. Secondary position update, step doubling,
per-primary `hash2(fract(ray_pos))` light/sky jitter, density call and weighted
accumulation are literal B15 source. Scattering/output/history code is untouched.
No texture operation or derivative changes scope. There is no new LOD policy,
sample reduction, transition smoothing or quality approximation.

Distance tiering still uses B15 cloud-shell entry distance divided by
`CLOUDS_SCALE` to convert atmosphere coordinates to camera-relative world blocks,
with the existing near/far/transition bands and all live presets. Secondary
lengths remain in the existing scaled cloud-coordinate units (B15 labels them
metres). The geometric-series extent correction is retained. Temporal upscale,
frame progression, sampling noise and cached-sky policy are unchanged.

`PHOTON_CLOUD_SECONDARY_EXTENT_PROBE` is an independent compile-time pack option,
default off. It has no new Java configuration or uniform transport. Off selects
the literal B15 parameter/math/call sites and emits no new helper/setup code.
The structural selector tests recover every affected B15 source member exactly
after selecting only probe directives away. An additional `original` arm keeps

## Risks and static evidence

Moving pure setup earlier preserves its semantic value, but changes when it is
evaluated. A cloud-shell ray with zero dense samples previously never called
the secondary function; a reduced-count ray now performs its two count-guarded
ratio setups before discovering that all samples are empty. Sparse rays may
therefore regress. Full-count rays avoid ratio evaluation, but still carry the
guarded source/control shape. Additional caller values can extend live ranges
and affect register pressure. The compiler might already hoist or specialize
the B15 expression. No shader disassembly, register count, occupancy or issued
exponential/texture count is available. Source cleanup cannot establish savings.

The CPU float32 model preserves expression association and finds identical
secondary sample coordinates, final positions and weighted analytical-density
outputs in 702 fixtures across positive advertised counts 1–12, reduced/equal
counts, layer lengths, sunrise/sunset factors and jitters. It uses CPU `exp2` and
a synthetic density field; it is not GLSL execution or Photon texture output.
Driver optimization can differ across program shapes, so mathematical/source
parity still requires real visual and timing checks.

## Consumer behavior and baseline

The original composite1 block calls `read_clouds_and_aurora(refracted_uv, ...)`
before checking `is_translucent || is_translucent_lod`. Its color is consumed only
inside that predicate and only when `clouds_apparent_distance < view_distance`.
The active arm places pixel-age `texelFetch`, filter-age arithmetic and cloud
color `textureLod` inside both existing predicates, directly before composition.
Vanilla and DH/Voxy translucency classification, refraction coordinates, alpha,
lightning intensity and blindness/darkness multiplication are preserved.

The apparent-distance `textureGather` remains at the outer Overworld scope.
The implicit-LOD lightning `texture(colortex12, ...)` stays at the same outer
scope under the original `LIGHTNING_FLASH_UNIFORM > 0.01` condition. Only its
result is consumed in the pixel-varying branch. No derivatives or explicit
gradients were invented, no early return/discard was introduced, and no
implicit-LOD texture operation was moved behind the translucency predicate.
The new branch contains only explicit-LOD/fetch operations and arithmetic.

`include/sky/clouds/sampling.glsl` remains byte-identical. Its original helper
still serves deferred terrain/sky, including rainbow behavior. Cloud generation,
temporal upscaling, history writes, near lighting, cloud marching, fog, AO,
shadow and water budgets are untouched. The old helper remains included in
composite1; driver dead-function/read elimination is not assumed or measured.

Distance continues in the original camera/view block units. Upstream
`program/d1_clouds.fsh` scales terrain distance with `CLOUDS_SCALE`, then stores
`result.apparent_distance * rcp(CLOUDS_SCALE)` in cloud data. Composite1 compares
the gathered/upscaled apparent distance to its existing `view_distance`; this
recipe preserves that conversion and comparison exactly. There is no new near,
far, transition or hysteresis boundary. Existing temporal filtering and
disocclusion behavior are retained; moving water/glass/cloud edges still need
runtime inspection.

The independent pack option is `PHOTON_CLOUD_CONSUMER_GUARD`, default off. It is
a compile-time shader control; no Java setting or live mod bridge controls it.
With the option undefined, the original cloud block is selected. The fixture
removes only experiment conditionals/declaration and recovers the original
member byte-for-byte; this is a structural check, not compiler evidence. The
`original` arm additionally leaves every upstream member's bytes untouched.
Each arm adds only its experiment provenance JSON outside the shader sources.

Pinned original `draw_cumulus_clouds` visits its original primary grid, skips

the complete light/sky optical-depth kernels: default six light density calls

approximation. Light/sky optical depths affect scattering, while primary density
and step length determine transmittance and apparent distance.

with extinction-weighted light/sky optical-depth differences no greater than
0.1. The first anchor has no such history, so reuse starts no earlier than
index 3. An empty primary cell invalidates the cache. Reuse never chains beyond
one cell. A failed guard evaluates the original full secondary counts and
updates history using those already-required samples.

Additional guards retain fresh lighting for moonlight, light elevation at or
below 0.2, forward scattering with view/light cosine at or above 0.8, invalid
projection/step/extinction inputs, density below 0.08, primary density changes
above 10%, layer altitude outside 0.1–0.9, or altitude changes above 0.05.
Finite-input checks retain full work. These comparisons add no texture probes.

Photon cloud coordinates use `CLOUDS_SCALE`. Sample distance and cell length
are divided by that value to obtain camera-relative world **blocks**. Secondary
kernel lengths stay in original scaled atmospheric coordinates. The private
distance weight rises from zero at 512 blocks to one at 1536 blocks. An
isotropic worst-orientation primary-cell screen extent is computed from
unchanged primary step length, projection scale, full output `view_res`, and
view depth. It has full weight at 32 output pixels or less and zero at 48
pixels or more. These thresholds are experimental heuristics, not a bound on
cloud illumination frequency or output error. They do not use derivatives.

The product of the two continuous weights is compared with a fixed screen
rank before the secondary kernels. This changes the fraction of odd cells
allowed to reuse across the distance/footprint transitions; it never evaluates
both light results to mix afterward. Quantization, the fixed screen pattern,
motion, checkerboard phase and TAA interaction remain quality risks. There is
no proven smooth motion transition.

Under identical sampling inputs, the source retains original primary density
and transmittance decisions. If Q occupied cells would evaluate lighting and R
eligible cells reuse, secondary density-call count changes from
`Q × (lighting_steps + ambient_steps)` to
`(Q − R) × (lighting_steps + ambient_steps)`, with `R <= floor(Q / 2)`.
This is a source call bound, not a GPU timing, texture-issue count or guaranteed
wavefront reduction. Divergence and register pressure can erase the benefit.

Each native key is exactly
`ivec2(clamp01(ray_pos) * view_res * taau_render_scale - 0.5)`, and the read is
`texelFetch(combined_depth_tex, texel, 0).x`. Without DH,
`combined_depth_tex` resolves to `depthtex1`; the actual export explicitly reads
`depthtex1`. Equality of that same key within the same invocation and unchanged
sampler/image domain permits exact scalar reuse. Integer level-zero reads do not
rely on implicit derivatives, normalized-coordinate nearest rounding or a
changed mip/filter. A cache would need its own valid flag and original first
fetch; depth zero cannot safely serve as an invalid-cache sentinel.

The native reconstruction uses **the current unquantized `ray_pos`**, not the
texel center: `screen_to_view_space(..., vec3(ray_pos, depth), true) - view_pos`.
Offset length, distance falloff, cosine and maximum horizon must therefore be
recomputed even after an equal-texel depth hit. Native arc integration, ambient
SSS, bent normal, multibounce correction, temporal accumulation and downstream
lighting/reflections remain necessary. Reusing a horizon result or skipping a
sample would violate the assigned exactness boundary.

## Natural footprint and overhead

Far GTAO radius tends to 1, making each native view-space horizon step
`GTAO_RADIUS / GTAO_HORIZON_STEPS = 2/3` block. Projected movement decreases with
distance; exact successive-texel equality remains dependent on both projected
components and texel phase. Reaching the far LOD band alone does not certify it.
Screen clamping can also produce repeated boundary keys; its natural frequency
in the coast scene was not measured.

For scale only, a center-view pinhole model at 1200 pixels tall and an **assumed**
70° vertical FOV has focal length about 857 pixels. A transverse 2/3-block step
falls below one pixel at about 571 blocks; for a 45° diagonal, both components
fall below one pixel at about 404 blocks. RD24 corresponds nominally to 384
blocks. These are analytical examples, not actual duplicate coverage or hard
visibility limits: no actual projection matrix, scene depths, radial slice
distribution, motion or clamped-sample frequency was collected. The original
receiver radius changes near the camera; native DH multiplies it by three for
LOD terrain and requires its own domain evidence.

A prior-depth cache adds key comparison, validity/control flow and live key/depth
state across iterations. A three-step horizon can save at most two of its three
reads with a local cache (eight of twelve across all four directions), while all
native reconstruction and lighting math remains. Extra cross-direction storage
or a new lookup structure would exceed this bounded premise. Source cannot
establish compiler lowering, register/spill cost, branch divergence, physical
memory savings, or whether existing texture caching already serves repeats.

[GPU summary](../../dev/logs/cross-shader-performance-r2/photon-original-cost-r2/gpu_samples-summary.json)

## A5 native validity and consumer contract

Pinned `program/d3_ao.fsh` calculates fresh AO at154–175, then gathers history
and validates previous UV/depth/age at183–238. It runs at .5 linear scale already.
The age caps at10 before depth/off-center weights; the final output may age11.
C6 RGBA16 stores AO, ambient SSS, bent-normal XY. C14 RG16F stores reversed

`world_age_changed` is declared in d3 but never used there. No native validation
covers material/normal changes, deformation, neighboring geometry or a resource

## Units, transition, optical meaning and fallback

Camera-relative `scene_pos` length is in world blocks. The reduction factor is
zero through 64 blocks and increases linearly to one at 112 blocks (48-block
transition). The unchanged clip-space filter radius divided by the positive
shadow projection X scale gives a world-space radius. A conservative maximum
main-projection X/Y scale converts that radius to full-resolution output pixels
using view depth. Projected radius at most 1 pixel permits the distance reduction;
1–2 pixels blends to original work; at least 2 pixels keeps original work.
Current render-scale changes therefore cannot make eligibility more aggressive.
Invalid distance, view depth, projection scale or radius retains original work.

The continuous control is quantized with `ceil` to integer tail counts. Counts
change by one at thresholds; there is no stochastic tier decision. TAA can hide
noise but cannot establish absence of motion flicker or threshold popping.

The original first four samples retain weight 1 and denominator N. Stratified
indices span the unchanged original outer annulus; each retained tail sample has
weight `(N - 4)/(M - 4)`. Final normalization remains division by original N.
Constant all-lit/all-shadow visibility and relative inner/outer annulus weights
are preserved. This is quadrature approximation: cast-shadow silhouettes,
foliage and thin shadows can still lose precision. It does not preserve arbitrary
shadow images exactly or certify the original upstream first-four certainty test.

Private option `SHADERLOD_SHADOW_BUDGET` defaults OFF. Its outer `#ifdef` is separate
from the inner program/world condition so pinned Iris discovers it. Private OFF
and all nonconsumer programs preprocess back to every original upstream member.
Private ON activates reduction only for bridge version exactly 2 and global
`shaderlodEnabled` exactly 1; unknown/absent versions, global OFF, nonzero SSS,

Private ON uses explicit `textureLod(shadowtex1, comparison_coord, 0.0)` for PCF

## Why internal-rate TAA cannot simply reuse final

A reusable architecture could accumulate temporal history at internal resolution
and spatially reconstruct once in an existing presentation pass. It would remove
c3 and avoid output-rate temporal processing. It gives up output-resolution
temporal detail, so sharper moving foliage and disocclusions are a quality risk.
For Photon the following contracts prevent a safe two-line adaptation:

- c4's `texel = gl_FragCoord * scale` is correct for its full-output draw. After
  shrinking c4 it would apply scale twice. History filtering, age lookup,
  offcenter rejection and clipping footprints would all need internal-space
  mapping and explicit clamps. `colortex5Clear=false` means stale pixels beyond
  the active rectangle must never enter any filter footprint.
- c4 alpha holds age except the bottom-left exposure texel. c4 vertex reads
  that same texel for exposure (`c4_taa_exposure.vsh:144`); it must remain exact.
  Screen-space reprojection and projection jitter are normalized scene
  coordinates, not stored-history coordinates. Their separation must survive
  startup, invalid bridge, scale switches and full reset handling.
- Bloom's first downsample reads **colortex5** with full-domain coordinates
  (`c5_c10_bloom_downsample.fsh:30–46`). Later tile layout is full-domain.
  Internal history requires remapped first-tile sampling and validated kernels.
- Full-output color grading directly fetches colortex5 by output texel
  (`c14_color_grading.fsh:189`) before bloom/tonemapping. Upscaling only at final
  leaves c14 reading stale history outside the internal rectangle. Reconstruct
  in c14, or move all downstream processing coherently to internal resolution;
  either is a different architecture with quality and filter obligations.
- A five-sample reconstruction in existing c14 would add four source samples
  per output pixel compared with its current center fetch. This can eat the
  saved c4 cost. Native CAS at final and optional FXAA also remain full-rate.
  There is no measured pass budget establishing a >5% ceiling.
- Photon final has a five-sample spatial branch when MC_RENDER_QUALITY differs
  from 1 (`final.fsh:278–283`), but pinned Iris hardcodes 1.0. Changing its macro
  alone does not resize attachments, scene rendering or the preceding graph.

Do not build a universal GLSL rewriting layer to solve these contracts. A later
explicit adapter would need a frozen supported graph and real consumer/lifetime
evidence first. Current cloud scale-transition quality remains independently
unaccepted; this proposal does not solve or supersede that work.

## Mechanism

Photon's `include/surface/water_normal.glsl:get_water_normal` computes three
wave heights at adjacent coordinates, subtracts them, and normalizes the result.
Each height evaluation samples one noise texture per wave octave and evaluates
one Gerstner-wave sine per octave. With height variation enabled, each height
also samples its variation texture. Existing ShaderLOD reduced octave counts
at distance but retained all three evaluations.

The candidate evaluates analytic wave slopes once for medium/far water. The
Gerstner height is `(0.5 + 0.5 sin(phi))^2`, so its spatial derivative with
locally constant noise is `(0.5 + 0.5 sin(phi)) cos(phi) * dphi/dcoord`.
The new `get_water_gradient` accumulates that derivative with the original
frequency, wavelength, amplitude, rotation and height normalization. It keeps
height variation as a multiplier. This avoids two thirds of the wave noise
texture fetches and two height evaluations in affected surface pixels. The
new gradient uses both sine and cosine, so the arithmetic reduction is smaller
than the texture/evaluation reduction and GPU benefit is unproven.

The noise texture derivative and slower height-variation derivative are omitted.
This changes distant normal detail and is an explicit approximation. It does
not flatten the water normal or modify geometric shadows/AO. It is unsuitable
for a claim of mathematically identical full-noise normals. Near, disabled and
shadow caustic paths keep the original three finite-difference heights and
original normalization expression. The branch selects one path before those
expensive evaluations; it does not evaluate both normals and blend afterward.

| `SHADERLOD_WATER_FAR` | 256 blocks | Center of medium-to-low transition. Fully low from 272 blocks. |

## Allocation, projection and complete consuming paths

Exact JAR `javap -p -c` outputs are retained in the study directory:

- `PackShadowDirectives.acceptDirectives` accepts the `shadowMapResolution`
  const-int directive; `ShadowRenderer` constructor stores that resolution.
- `ShadowRenderTargets` creates main and no-translucents depth textures at
  R × R; its lazy color targets use the same dimensions. The exact hardware
  depth format/bytes are not inferred from the generic `DEPTH` request.
- `ShadowRenderer.setShadowViewport` sets R × R. `copyPreTranslucentDepth`
  uses R × R for either framebuffer blit or the selected depth copy strategy.
  Pixel-area reduction can reduce raster, clear and copy traffic, but not the
  submitted caster set, terrain/entity traversal or shadow vertex count.
- Orthographic projection is constructed from shadow distance and near/far
  planes, independently of resolution. `ShadowMatrices.createOrthoMatrix`
  uses a symmetric width/height of twice the half-plane length. Model-view
  snapping uses the independent 2-block interval; this study changes neither.
- `StandardMacros` defines `MC_SHADOW_QUALITY` as **1.0** in this exact Iris
  JAR. Photon uses R × this macro for integer texel addressing. Do not assume
  this remains true in OptiFine or another Iris version.

## Filtering and quality implications

PCSS lines 26–27 use `shadow_map_pixel_size = 1/R`. Minimum PCF radius is
`2/R * distortion_factor`; without VPS, penumbra is
`sqrt(0.5)/R * penumbraScale * (1 + 7*sss_amount)` (lines 103 and 252–256).
Their ratio cancels R. Therefore the canonical configuration's requested PCF
sample count is algebraically unchanged by reducing R; the original first-four
lit/shadow exits remain. Twenty arithmetic fixtures confirm this cancellation
across all supported resolutions, representative SSS and distortion factors;
GLSL floating-point threshold behavior and driver early exits are unmeasured.

2048 → 1536 retains 56.25% of atlas texels, removes 43.75%, and increases minimum
world-space filtering support by **33.33%** at the same local projection.
1024 would remove 75% and double that support; start with 1536. Nonlinear
0.85 distortion makes world-space texels nonuniform. The ideal center local
texel width is roughly `256 * 0.15 / R`, or 0.01875 → 0.025 blocks, not a
uniform bound over the atlas or a screen-space quality guarantee.

Distance/domain and distant SSRT/lightmap transition remain at 128 blocks
(`shadows/common.glsl:6`, deferred4 near/distant blend). This preserves the
presence of distant lighting cues in source, not their perceptual equivalence.
Bias (`distortion.glsl:43–45`) does not grow with texels; lower resolution can
expose acne/leaks, unstable alpha-tested leaves, missing thin shadows, changed
contact softness and temporal shimmer. VL rays sample coarser depth and can
change shaft edges. VPS-on configurations instead have a world-scaled blocker
radius and penumbra; their PCF count can change as minimum texel radius grows.
They require a separate calibration. Do not tune penumbra scale simultaneously
or claim this stock control preserves a fixed physical penumbra.

This differs from the rejected distant PCF tail prototype:
[review](PHOTON_SHADOW_BUDGET_REVIEW.md) rejected its grazing-receiver footprint
bound before runtime. That path reduced receiver samples without map changes;
this study does not revive it. Shadow list/coherence/cadence studies are also
separate; resolution does not remove their CPU work or authorize cached maps.

## Plausible cost ceiling and short next experiment

The latest actual bracket exports only 241 `game-render` GPU rows for original
native-before, not a shadow-map decomposition. Thus **current atlas cost is
unknown**. Historical CPU shadow scopes or nested/interleaved GPU attribution
are not additive whole-frame shares. There is no measured numeric cost ceiling.

An explicitly hypothetical model is `saving = (1 - (1536/2048)^2) * S =
0.4375 * S`, where S is resolution-sensitive atlas raster/copy cost and every
other cost is fixed. Vertex/submission costs do not scale with map area; cache
benefits or hardware saturation can also depart from this model. At the live
pixel arm's 15.2448 ms frame/13.9006 ms GPU, a 10% GPU share would save only
0.608 ms (about 4.15% FPS if this reduced frame time equally). Adding 5% FPS
would require S ≈ 1.659 ms; lifting an illustrative 1.09× original result to
1.20× would require S ≈ 3.194 ms. These are screening thresholds, not expected
or proven savings, and combined candidate gains cannot be multiplied blindly.

## Cache and numerical constraints

Cache initialization is invalid and nonsmooth. Every even primary index is
fresh; reuse is only possible on an odd index. The first fresh occupied cell
establishes validity but cannot establish smoothness. A later fresh occupied
cell compares direct/sky depths against the previous cached depths. Therefore
the earliest possible reuse is primary index 3 and needs at least three occupied
cells including the candidate. An empty cell clears both flags. Nonfinite fresh
depths invalidate history; a reused cell does not update its even anchor. No
cache survives an empty gap and no two consecutive cells can reuse.

With only Q known, the conservative ray bound is
`R ≤ max(0, floor((Q − 1) / 2))`. Summed over the actual sampled Q values, its
upper bound is 192 reused pairs; actual R is zero. This is a loose source ceiling
for these observed counts, not predicted savings, positive coverage or a frame
cost budget. Unknown occupied-cell placement and all numerical guards can lower
it, including to zero.

Ray-wide eligibility requires nonmoonlit lighting, `light_dir.y > 0.2`,
`dot(ray_dir, light_dir) < 0.8`, finite positive pixel scale, view cosine,
step length and extinction. Per-cell eligibility requires finite values,
distance > 512 blocks, footprint in [0, 48) output pixels, both current and
anchor densities ≥ 0.08 with ≤ 10% relative difference, both altitudes in
[0.1, 0.9] with difference ≤ 0.05, then
`rank < clamp((distance − 512) / 1024) × clamp((48 − footprint) / 16)`.
Full distance weight begins at 1536 blocks; full footprint weight is at or below
32 output pixels. Cached fresh direct and sky depth differences, multiplied by
extinction, must both be finite and at most 0.1.

Footprint uses full-output `view_res`, not the 744 × 418 trace extent:
`cell_blocks × pixel_scale / max(distance_blocks × view_cosine, 0.0001)`.
Substituting the quarter-size trace dimensions would change the quality guard;
this audit does not recommend it. These local/prior-history predicates do not
bound unseen remote cloud shadows. The existing review's remote-occluder risk
remains unresolved, even if a later diagnostic observes reuse.
